symptom_fingerprint: The configured route never produced a real pending approval, so no live decision could be sent
hypothesis: A thread created with allow_shell true, trust_mode false and auto_approve false will pause for approval before a shell command
action: Started the pinned runtime from a throwaway home and submitted one turn that must run bash; recorded every event
result: Turn submission returned HTTP 400: the throwaway home has no provider key, so no turn ran. Nothing about approvals was observed.

symptom_fingerprint: The configured route never produced a real pending approval, so no live decision could be sent
hypothesis: Running the same turn against the machine's own engine home, with the thread in posture ask and auto_approve false, will emit approval.required before the bash tool runs
action: Repeated the round trip with the real engine home and a throwaway workspace; subscribed to every event and recorded tool use
result: The thread reported permission_posture ask, bash ran, and the turn completed with no approval.required, approval.decided or approval.timeout event; the reply routes were still proven by typed refusals for unknown ids

symptom_fingerprint: The configured route never produced a real pending approval, so no live decision could be sent
hypothesis: The saved permission_posture=full-access in the engine settings caps thread- and turn-level auto_approve/trust_mode, so no prompt can be produced without changing the user's saved posture
action: Read the engine's own strings and the machine settings read-only: settings.toml records full-access, and the binary documents that auto_approve, trust_mode and allow_shell are capped by the configured approval policy
result: Root cause identified without changing user configuration; a live approval needs the human to switch the saved posture to ask for one probe, which is a user configuration decision, not an engineering one

symptom_fingerprint: The committed mona.ico did not decode (Electron nativeImage empty; Windows reads type 256/count 1792) and Mona.exe still carried Electron's icon group
hypothesis: The ICO container was written big-endian, and staging renamed electron.exe without touching its PE resources
action: Rewrote the ICO container little-endian, added tools/assets/embed-exe-icon.mjs and called it from buildStage; verified with Windows ExtractIconEx and a PE resource read-back
result: ICO decodes at 256 px in Electron; installed Mona.exe carries all seven approved images byte-identical; shell-extracted 16/32 px match generated PNGs exactly
